Answers the user's question on splitting allocation between generated code and the runtime: fixed-size allocations become inline recipes on the existing recipe table, with one shared bump and one cold runtime entry that finds room. Projected (unmeasured): enum −11%, msg −5%, distiller −1.7%. Builder: GC. Step I4.

comments.text: PR #811 rebased after #803. Bench: reqrep −1.8%, ring −0.65%, maps and fanin −0.5% (17–21 instructions per box); nothing rises. SCOPE NARROWED from the approved page: constant bitstrings (compiled code never allocated them) and static views (retain off-heap state) stay runtime calls, as do boxes made in receive-dispatch bodies (entered from Rust). The narrowing awaits the user's word.

GC's answers on the scope. (a) Constant bitstrings: nothing to move. Compiled code never calls fz_alloc_bitstring_const; only the interpreter does (ir_interp/value.rs:268). A small literal is a static object (prim.rs static_object_ref), and a large one takes the static-view path. (b) Static views: the page's own condition, 'if the BinRef isn't static, the view stays a call', applies. fz_alloc_binview_from_static (ir_runtime.rs:1424) retains the SharedBin and allocates a heap BinRef. GC proposes 'A large binary literal is static data' under fz-9e2, blocked by 9e2.4. Receive-dispatch boxes are a real gap, about 0.65% of ring. GC proposes 'A box made in a receive dispatch body is placed inline' under fz-9x7.41. Both proposals await the user.

Closing note (GC, 2026-11-20): compiled code never allocated constant bitstrings, so that part of the original title was moot; static views move to fz-9e2.15. Receive dispatch bodies' boxes are fz-9x7.41.6.
